title: Describing things
goal: Describe people and things by colour, size, age and quality, and compare them (bigger, the biggest).
intro: Good news: Odia adjectives **never change** — not for gender, not for plural, not for case. Put them before the noun, or after it as the description. Comparison is just as simple: *X Y-than big* = 'X is bigger than Y'.

phrases.en: The tea is very hot, careful!

grammar.title: Adjectives don't change
grammar.body:
An adjective goes **before** the noun it describes and stays exactly the same whatever the noun: ନାଲି ଶାଢ଼ୀ 'a red saree', ନାଲି ଶାଢ଼ୀଗୁଡ଼ିକ 'the red sarees', ନାଲି ଶାଢ଼ୀରେ 'in a red saree'. There is no gender agreement as in Hindi (*lāl sāṛī / baṛā laṛkā / baṛī laṛkī*) — Odia simply says ବଡ଼ ପୁଅ, ବଡ଼ ଝିଅ.

To describe, put the adjective at the end with no verb: ଘରଟି ପୁରୁଣା 'the house [is] old'. For a temporary state use ଅଛି: ପାଣି ଥଣ୍ଡା ଅଛି 'the water is cold (now)'.

Intensifiers: **ବହୁତ** 'very', colloquial **ଭାରି** 'really', **ଟିକେ** 'a bit'.

examples.en: He/She is tall; his/her brother is short.
The Odia language is really sweet.
The new books are on the table.

grammar.title: Comparison: ଠାରୁ (than) and ସବୁଠାରୁ (most)
grammar.body:
To compare, put **-ଠାରୁ** (*-ṭharu*, colloquially **-ଠୁ**) after the thing you compare *with*, then the adjective: *A B-than big* = 'A is bigger than B'. You can add **ଅଧିକ** 'more' for emphasis: B-ଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ସୁନ୍ଦର 'more beautiful than B'. (Formal writing uses **ଅପେକ୍ଷା**.)

The superlative is **ସବୁଠାରୁ** + adjective — literally 'than all': ସବୁଠାରୁ ବଡ଼ 'the biggest'.

'As … as / like' uses **ପରି**: ତା ପରି ଲମ୍ବା 'as tall as him'. With a negative: … ପରି ନୁହେଁ 'not as … as'.

examples.native: ମୋ ଭାଇ ମୋଠାରୁ ଦୁଇ ବର୍ଷ ବଡ଼।
examples.roman: mo bhai moṭharu dui bôrsô bôṛô.
examples.en: My brother is two years older than me.

examples.native: ଏ ରାସ୍ତା ସେ ରାସ୍ତାଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ସଫା।
examples.roman: e rasta se rastaṭharu ôdhikô sôpha.
examples.en: This road is cleaner than that road.
The Mahanadi is Odisha's biggest river.

examples.native: ଏ ଚା ସେ ଚା ପରି ମିଠା ନୁହେଁ।
examples.roman: e cha se cha pôri miṭha nuheṃ.
examples.en: This tea isn't as sweet as that tea.

dialogue.title: Choosing a saree
dialogue.setting: Sam wants to buy a saree for his mother; Lipi helps him in a handloom shop.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ମୁଁ ମୋ ମା ପାଇଁ ଗୋଟିଏ ଶାଢ଼ୀ ନେବାକୁ ଚାହେଁ।
lines.roman: muṃ mo ma paiṃ goṭie saṛhi nebaku chaheṃ.
lines.en: I want to get a saree for my mother.

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.native: ବହୁତ ଭଲ କଥା। ସମ୍ବଲପୁରୀ ଶାଢ଼ୀ ନିଅ। ସେଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଭାରି ସୁନ୍ଦର।
lines.roman: bôhutô bhôlô kôtha. Sômbôlôpuri saṛhi niô. seguṛikô bhari sundôrô.
lines.en: Lovely idea. Get a Sambalpuri saree. They're really beautiful.

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.native: ତୁମ ମାଙ୍କୁ କେଉଁ ରଙ୍ଗ ଭଲ ଲାଗେ?
lines.roman: tumô maṅku keuṃ rôṅgô bhôlô lage?
lines.en: Which colour does your mother like?

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.native: ଏହି ନେଳି ଶାଢ଼ୀଟି ଦେଖ। ଏହାର ପାଢ଼ ନାଲି।
lines.roman: ehi neḷi saṛhiṭi dekhô. eharô paṛhô nali.
lines.en: Look at this blue saree. Its border is red.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ସୁନ୍ଦର! କିନ୍ତୁ ସେ ସବୁଜଟି ଏହାଠାରୁ ହାଲୁକା।
lines.roman: sundôrô! kintu se sôbujôṭi ehaṭharu haluka.
lines.en: Beautiful! But that green one is lighter than this.

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.native: ହଁ, ଖରାଦିନ ପାଇଁ ହାଲୁକା ଶାଢ଼ୀ ଭଲ।
lines.roman: hôṃ, khôradinô paiṃ haluka saṛhi bhôlô.
lines.en: Yes, a light saree is better for the hot season.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Then I'll take the green one.

culture: Odisha is famous for handloom: **ସମ୍ବଲପୁରୀ** *ikat* sarees with their tie-dyed patterns, **ବୋମକାଇ**, and Cuttack's silver filigree (*tarakasi*). Colours carry meaning: white is worn for mourning, red and yellow are auspicious for weddings and festivals.

tip.title: Adjectives stay the same
tip.body:
- The adjective goes **before** the noun and never changes: ନାଲି ଶାଢ଼ୀ, ନାଲି ଗାଡ଼ି, ନାଲି ଶାଢ଼ୀଗୁଡ଼ିକ.
- To describe, put it at the end with no verb: ମୋ ଗାଡ଼ି ଧଳା 'my car is white'.
- Ask a colour with **କି**: ଏହା କି ରଙ୍ଗ? 'what colour is it?'
- Make it stronger with **ବହୁତ** very, **ଭାରି** really; softer with **ଟିକେ** a bit.

sentences.native: ହଳଦିଆ ଆମ୍ବ ମିଠା, ସବୁଜ ଆମ୍ବ ଖଟା।
sentences.roman: hôḷôdia ambô miṭha, sôbujô ambô khôṭa.
sentences.en: Yellow mangoes are sweet; green mangoes are sour.

sentences.native: କମଳା ରଙ୍ଗ ମୋତେ ଭଲ ଲାଗେ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: kômôḷa rôṅgô mote bhôlô lage nahiṃ.

tip.title: 'Which?' and 'or'
tip.body:
- **କେଉଁ** = which: କେଉଁ ରଙ୍ଗ? 'which colour?'
- **ନା** between two choices = 'or': ନୂଆ **ନା** ପୁରୁଣା? 'new or old?'
- **ପ୍ରିୟ** = favourite: ମୋର ପ୍ରିୟ ରଙ୍ଗ 'my favourite colour'.
- In speech **ଭାରି** means 'really': ଭାରି ସୁନ୍ଦର! 'really beautiful!'

sentences.native: କେଉଁ ଶାଢ଼ୀ ସୁନ୍ଦର, ନାଲି ନା ନେଳି?
sentences.roman: keuṃ saṛhi sundôrô, nali na neḷi?
sentences.en: Which saree is nicer, the red or the blue?
Is the car new or old?
Will you have tea or milk?

sentences.native: ଆମ ଘର ପୁରୁଣା, କିନ୍ତୁ ଭାରି ସୁନ୍ଦର।
sentences.roman: amô ghôrô puruṇa, kintu bhari sundôrô.
sentences.en: Our house is old, but really lovely.
Bhubaneswar is a really beautiful city.

tip.title: Comparing: -ଠାରୁ and ସବୁଠାରୁ
tip.body:
- 'A is bigger than B': A + B**ଠାରୁ** + adjective: ପୁରୀ କଟକଠାରୁ ଛୋଟ. Add **ଅଧିକ** for 'more': ଏହାଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ମିଠା.
- 'The most': **ସବୁଠାରୁ** + adjective: ସବୁଠାରୁ ଲମ୍ବା 'the tallest'.
- 'As … as / like': **ପରି**: ତା ବୋଉ ପରି ସୁନ୍ଦର; 'not as': … ପରି ନୁହେଁ.
- Pronouns: ମୋଠାରୁ 'than me', ତୁମଠାରୁ 'than you'.

sentences.en: My sister is taller than me.
My friend is thinner than me.
This room is smaller than that one.
Is there one smaller than this?

sentences.native: ଏ ଆମ୍ବ ସେ ଆମ୍ବଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ମିଠା।
sentences.roman: e ambô se ambôṭharu ôdhikô miṭha.
sentences.en: This mango is sweeter than that one.
I'm the tallest in my family.
Lipi is as pretty as her mum.

sentences.native: ଏ ଚା ବୋଉଙ୍କ ଚା ପରି ନୁହେଁ।
sentences.roman: e cha bouṅkô cha pôri nuheṃ.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଗେଡ଼ା, କିନ୍ତୁ ମୋ ବାପା ବହୁତ ଲମ୍ବା।
sentences.roman: muṃ geṛa, kintu mo bapa bôhutô lômba.
sentences.en: I'm short, but my dad is very tall.

tip.title: Feeling hot or cold
tip.body:
- A thing's state right now can take ଅଛି: ପାଣି ଥଣ୍ଡା ଅଛି 'the water is cold (now)'.
- *You* feeling hot or cold uses the to-me form: **ମୋତେ ଥଣ୍ଡା ଲାଗୁଛି** 'I feel cold', ମୋତେ ଗରମ ଲାଗୁଛି 'I feel hot'.
- **ହୋଇଗଲା** 'has become': ଚା ଥଣ୍ଡା ହୋଇଗଲା 'the tea has gone cold'.

sentences.native: ମୋତେ ଥଣ୍ଡା ଲାଗୁଛି, ଝରକା ବନ୍ଦ କର।
sentences.roman: mote thôṇḍa laguchhi, jhôrôka bôndô kôrô.
sentences.en: I feel cold — close the window. (familiar)
Switch on the fan — it's very hot.

tip.title: Broken, heavy, light
tip.body:
- **ଖରାପ** = bad, and also broken or not working: ପଙ୍ଖା ଖରାପ ହୋଇଯାଇଛି 'the fan has broken'.
- **ହୋଇଯାଇଛି / ହୋଇଗଲା** 'has become' describes a change.
- **ଭାରି** = heavy (and, in speech, 'really'); **ହାଲୁକା** = light, in weight or colour: ହାଲୁକା ନେଳି 'light blue'.
- **-ଟି** on a noun = 'the': କୋଠରୀଟି, ଗିଲାସଟି.

sentences.en: My bag is light — I'll carry it.

sentences.native: ଗିଲାସଟି ସଫା ନାହିଁ, ଆଉ ଗୋଟିଏ ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ।
sentences.roman: gilasôṭi sôpha nahiṃ, au goṭie diôntu.
sentences.en: The glass isn't clean — please give me another.
This water is bad — don't drink it. (familiar)

sentences.native: ହାଲୁକା ନେଳି ରଙ୍ଗ ମୋତେ ଭଲ ଲାଗେ।
sentences.roman: haluka neḷi rôṅgô mote bhôlô lage.
